solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Question papers ready?

definitions.note: the ready is slang for cash, and a quid is a pound coin or note

parts.note: ID, identity papers or documents

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the exam papers have been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like 'prepared' but is British slang for money; a quid is one pound sterling, so the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money in hand; one pound sterling is an example of such cash.

clue.text: Light drink downed by fellow in one

indicators.note: in means the drinking fellow is placed inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one

indicators.note: downed means swallowed, so the drink goes inside the fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A light drink swallowed by a man in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a description of the drink but is the definition, meaning trivial; 'downed by' and 'in' are both containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Light in the sense of trivial or of little weight or consequence.

clue.text: Academic qualification showing kid up to speed

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to cod is to kid or hoax
taken as written
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A qualification proving a youngster is up to speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to tease, COD; 'up' turns it to DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A PhD or similar higher degree is an academic qualification.

clue.text: Drink sparkling wine with ricotta? Not I

indicators.note: sparkling suggests the letters fizzing about and settling in a new order
Not tells us to leave out the letter I, which the clue names directly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu pairing: bubbly wine served alongside ricotta cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkling' looks like a description of the wine but shuffles WINE and RICOTTA once 'Not I' has removed one I.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonated mixer flavoured with quinine is a drink, often served with gin.

clue.text: Social networker using rather cute short name

parts.note: twee means excessively cute

indicators.note: short means the word for name loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A social media user picks a cute abbreviated handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short name' looks like a nickname but is TERM cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone posting on Twitter is a user of a social network.

clue.text: Change trains? One might, crossing tip of English county

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters go across, round, the single letter
change says the letters are rearranged
the tip here is the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A passenger wonders whether to change trains on a journey into an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like an instruction to the traveller but is the anagram signal; 'tip of English' is its last letter, H, not the E a solver first reaches for, and 'crossing' puts the anagram round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Notts is a county in the East Midlands of England, home of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Head of organisation is in control, and that's official

indicators.note: is in means the leading letter goes inside the word for control

parts.note: to corner a market is to control it

indicators.note: the head is the first letter

explanation.surface: The boss of a company has taken charge, and it is now formal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'official' looks like an adjective meaning formal but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer who investigates sudden deaths is a public official.

clue.text: City, one in grip of revolution

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it

parts.note: a turn is one revolution
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city held fast by a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising but means a rotation, TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, Torino in Italian, is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Lover boy runs rings around me

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: around means the two rings surround the word me

parts.note: two rings look like two O letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic young man circles around the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs rings around' reads as an idiom for outdoing someone, but splits into three separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lover gave his name to any amorous man.

clue.text: Rifle we must store in box, right?

indicators.note: storing something means holding it inside, so the word we wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A gun owner asks whether the rifle should be locked away in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must store' makes the word we hold the next two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is a famous make of American repeating rifle, so the brand names the gun.

clue.text: No end of publicity for concert

indicators.note: losing its end means the word for publicity drops its final letter

parts.note: a promo is a promotional piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A concert that is getting a huge amount of publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as 'plenty of' but cuts the last O from PROMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prom is one of the Promenade Concerts held each summer at London's Royal Albert Hall.

clue.text: Develop as writer whose son's gone to the front

indicators.note: going to the front means a letter shifts to the start of the writer's name

parts.note: Marcel Proust, the French novelist

explanation.surface: Someone grows as an author after their son has been sent off to fight at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to the front' sounds military but moves the S of PROUST to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow or put out shoots is to develop, as a seed does.

clue.text: Pub open? Drug available within, it's suggested

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: available within means the drug is placed inside the word for open

parts.note: to undo something is to open it
E stands for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A bar is open and drugs can be had inside, so people hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available within' puts the drug inside the word for open; E for ecstasy is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation is something hinted at rather than said outright, a suggestion.

clue.text: We sell cheaper food, though not hot chips

indicators.note: though not means the letter for hot is left out

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
counters are gaming chips

explanation.surface: A cheap food shop boasts, though it serves no hot chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' looks like fries but means gaming tokens. The definition speaks as the shops themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops that cut prices describe themselves this way, as businesses selling below the usual rate.

clue.text: Sea creature half-visible from Orkney

indicators.note: only half being visible means just the first half of the word is shown

parts.note: an Orcadian is a person or thing from Orkney

explanation.surface: A sea animal glimpsed off the Orkney islands, half above the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Orkney' gives ORCADIAN, a word solvers may not know, and 'half-visible' keeps its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a marine mammal, a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Lacking consideration, come what may

definitions.meaning: without paying regard or heed to something

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtless who pushes on whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is heedless, without regard; the other is anyway, despite everything.

clue.text: Maybe one hot guy being entertained by uncle lavishly

indicators.note: being entertained by means being taken inside, as a guest is
lavishly suggests the letters spread about freely into a new order

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, a guy

explanation.surface: An attractive young man is being treated generously by his uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lavishly' shuffles the uncle to LUNCE, and 'being entertained by' takes the hot guy inside. One o'clock exemplifies the midday meal hour.
explanation.definitionFit: One o'clock is a typical hour for the midday meal, so it exemplifies the time.

clue.text: A place to rest when training outside for cross-country event

indicators.note: outside means the training letters go round the rest of the pieces

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
taken as written
a perch is where a bird rests
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Runners in training rest somewhere outdoors before a cross-country race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the training letters round everything else; PE is physical education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare-and-hounds race where runners follow a trail of torn paper across country.

clue.text: Irritating member of audience in box speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the word for box is said out loud

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox

explanation.surface: An annoying theatregoer sitting up in one of the boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a theatre box but is COFFER, which said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a hacking cough disturbs a concert or play, irritating others in the audience.

clue.text: Royal attendant really blowing top, having to guard queen repeatedly

indicators.note: guarding means holding inside, so the queen letters go within
blowing its top means losing the first letter

parts.note: very means really
queen given twice in different abbreviations, QU and ER

explanation.surface: A royal servant loses his temper while protecting the Queen again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' suggests rage but cuts V from VERY to give ERY; 'having to guard' puts QU and ER inside it. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the royal household who attends members of the royal family.

clue.text: Seconds of onion soup available when it's 16?

indicators.note: the second letters of each of the next two words are taken

parts.note: on means available, as in a dish being on today

explanation.surface: Second helpings of onion soup are on offer at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like second helpings; it picks N and O. The definition refers to 16 Down, the answer LUNCHTIME: midday is when people often eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a common time for the midday meal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Robberies on the increase among crooks

indicators.note: among means the rising word is put inside the word for crooks

parts.note: a shepherd's crook is a stick
up means rising, on the increase

explanation.surface: Robberies are rising among criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' reads as criminals but means shepherds' sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed hold-ups are robberies, where the victim is made to raise their hands.

clue.text: Secure, oddly enough, with only one small coin in purse

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
P is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Keeping just one small coin safe in a purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purse' is an archaic sense: a scrip was a small bag or wallet carried by pilgrims.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a satchel or small bag, as carried by a pilgrim or shepherd.

clue.text: Port is overlooking lake, so we're told

indicators.note: so we're told means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: IS placed above MERE, a lake; in a down clue the upper piece overlooks the lower

explanation.surface: A harbour town is said to stand above a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the words come out as the name of Turkey's third-largest city, a port on the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: Once called Smyrna, this is a major seaport on Turkey's Aegean coast.

clue.text: Release a foreign worker

parts.note: un is French for a
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A migrant labourer is set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To take one's hands off someone is to let them go, a dated word for releasing.

clue.text: Cut of beef no good

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is removed from the word for beef

parts.note: a beef or grump is a complaint

explanation.surface: A butcher dismisses a joint of beef as poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but means a complaint, GRUMP; 'Cut of beef' wants to be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is a cut of meat from the hindquarters.

clue.text: Hitchcock's first appearance at what's announced as cutting-edge horror film?

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the director's name

parts.note: air can mean appearance or manner

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a razor has a cutting edge

explanation.surface: Alfred Hitchcock's cameo in an innovative horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting-edge' looks like 'innovative' but gives RAZOR, which said aloud sounds like RAISER.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening film makes the hair stand up, so it is an example of a horror movie.

clue.text: Missing ace serve, player stumbles awkwardly

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters falling about into a new order
missing means the letter for ace is left out of the fodder

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A tennis player misses an ace serve and trips clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbles' shuffles SERVE PLAYER once 'Missing' has taken out A, 'ace' in tennis misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting contrarily or in a wrong-headed way is behaving awkwardly.

clue.text: Language writer seldom uses

indicators.note: uses means the clue words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A tongue that authors rarely write in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' signals the answer sits inside 'writER SEldom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish or Scottish Gaelic, a Celtic tongue, is called this.
